To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
global reasoning is useful for pose generation, and that we can formulate a novel CRF with a new optimization scheme to do so efficiently.

i) the global CRF is able to select a single pose-hypothesis from a very large pool of hypotheses and ii) this global approach is able to outperform the state-of-the-art on the Occluded Object Dataset, which is a very challenging benchmark.

global reasoning is superior to local reasoning in the generation of pose hypotheses, and that a CRF with non-Gaussian potential functions can be optimized in a two-step procedure that has some guarantees for optimizality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two aspects: i) the first global reasoning for the task of 6D-predict, ii) a new efficient optimization procedure for non-Gaussian CRF.
the task of estimating object 6D pose from RGBD images.
the problem of 6D pose estimation of known 3D objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach outperforms all existing approaches in terms of both, accuracy and efficiency.
global reasoning for pose generation is beneficial and should be used in conjunction with local reasoning.
our approach is the best method for 6D pose estimation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose the first fully-connected CRF for pose estimation, and show how it can be used in a global reasoning framework to improve performance.
we show that global reasoning can be successfully employed for pose estimation and we give a practical algorithm that achieves this.
we show that global reasoning can be beneficial for the task of 6D object pose estimation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to achieve the best performance, the hypotheses generation step must be done in a global manner.
global reasoning is a viable alternative to local reasoning for pose estimation.
global reasoning can be very beneficial for the second step of the pose-estimation pipeline, even though the CRF is trained on synthetic data only.
